scientific_claim: For the declared lattice experiment family: CFM and projected local-MC respond similarly to interface-angle rotation, indicating a shared finite interface-projection artifact rather than a learned-kernel artifact. No configuration is certified because the required robustness evidence or acceptance gates are incomplete.
claim_scope: The declared two-dimensional benchmark family, controlled action set, checkpoints, sample counts, angular rotations, and random seeds only.

action.hypothesis: The coarse interface quadrature establishes the reference sensitivity before any mitigation.
A quarter-bin interface-angle rotation isolates direction locking in CFM and projected local-MC.
A quarter-bin dense-S_N rotation isolates quadrature-locked rays in the deterministic comparator.
A matched seed repeat estimates the stochastic floor of CFM and projected local-MC comparisons.
Increasing only face-position resolution tests whether midpoint compression creates artifacts.
Rotating the position-refined interface grid tests whether its apparent improvement is orientation robust.
A new seed estimates stochastic response-construction variability for the position-refined candidate.
Increasing only azimuthal resolution at the same state budget as position refinement tests angular causality.
Rotating the angularly refined interface grid tests whether angular refinement removes grid locking.
A new seed estimates stochastic response-construction variability for the angularly refined candidate.
Joint position and azimuthal refinement should reduce shared interface projection sensitivity.
A rotated joint-refinement run verifies that the candidate is not merely aligned with one angular grid.
A new seed tests whether the joint-refinement result exceeds the stochastic operator-construction floor.
Increasing only dense-S_N azimuthal order tests whether its visible rays are finite-angle artifacts.
Rotating the refined dense-S_N quadrature tests residual orientation sensitivity after angular refinement.
Global Monte Carlo tests whether the cheapest coarse candidate preserves physical flux levels.
Global Monte Carlo tests whether the position-refined candidate preserves physical flux levels.
Global Monte Carlo tests whether the angularly refined candidate preserves physical flux levels.
High-statistics global Monte Carlo checks that the robust candidate preserves physical flux levels.

limitations: A directional residual between two fields does not identify which field contains the artifact.
Rotation sensitivity is a causal numerical diagnostic, not a universal physical observable.
Projected local-MC shares the same finite interface phase space and isolates learned-kernel error only.
Dense S_N is a finite-angle deterministic diagnostic and is not treated as continuum truth.
Global history MC is a physical certification reference only at statistically supported tallies.
A recommendation is withheld unless matched rotation evidence and all declared acceptance gates pass.
